en: Taal Volcano is an island located inside a crater lake, which itself sits inside the caldera of a much larger volcano.
Mount Mayon in Albay is famous for having the most perfectly symmetrical cone shape of any active volcano in the entire world.
The Rafflesia, found in Philippine rainforests, produces the largest individual flower in the world, growing three feet across and smelling like rotting meat.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao are carved into steep mountains and, if laid end to end, would stretch halfway around the entire globe.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan flows directly into the sea, making it a unique navigable underground river with a massive cave system.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 perfectly symmetrical cone-shaped hills that magically turn brown during the dry summer season.
The Tubbataha Reef in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site that is completely submerged and only accessible by boat for three months yearly.
The Philippines sits in the Coral Triangle, containing the highest marine biodiversity on Earth and protecting over 600 different species of colorful corals.
Palawan is the longest province in the Philippines, stretching over 400 kilometers and acting as a vital biological corridor connecting the country to Borneo.
The San Juanico Bridge connects the islands of Leyte and Samar and features a unique, beautifully curved marine viaduct design spanning over two kilometers.
The Philippines holds the world's largest known deposits of nickel and is also among the top countries globally for massive gold and copper reserves.
The Philippine eagle, one of the largest and strongest eagles on Earth, possesses a unique shaggy crest and can only be found in the wild Philippines.
